- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 76+), often overshooting by 2–5 points and failing to correct downward.
- Shows persistent lag in responding to recent price drops — forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model fails to adjust downward when prices are above historical mean (e.g., 75+), and overestimates when prices are below mean.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true outcomes — model under-reacts to volatility, especially in mid-to-late periods.
- In cases with strong downward trends, model fails to recognize the slope and underestimates the drop rate.
- When true prices are below 65, model often overcorrects upward, suggesting a ceiling bias in low-price zones.
- Forecasts are generally too optimistic in the final 5–7 days — model tends to “climb” toward higher values even when true prices are declining.
